title: Mani and the rise of Manichaeism
summary: Mani, born in 216 in Persian Babylonia, had revelations from age 12 and at 24 received a calling as an apostle of light. He left his community, preached in Persia, travelled to northern India in the early 240s and returned after Shapur I took the throne, who let him teach. Executed in 276 under Bahram I, his teachings reached North Africa in the west and the China Sea in the east.

uncertainty.note: Beth Mardutho gives Shapur I as 242-72 and Mani's death ca. 276; the University of Washington essay gives Shapur I as r. 241-272 and Mani executed in 276. Start 242 follows the royal-protection date; birth was 216.

as_recorded.value: royal protection of Shapur I (242-72); Mani was put to death ca. 276
returned shortly after the coronation of Shapur I (r. 241-272); executed in 276

importance.justification: Founded a religion that spread from North Africa to the China Sea within a few generations.
